text:
maria: Heads up — after we flipped the dynamic kernel selector to prefer quantized kernels for short layers, 2xA100 inference runs show a reproducible throughput regression (~11%) and p50 token latency increase (~28ms). It smells like an all-reduce / channel interaction when kernels change mid-sequence. Anyone seen channel drift like this? :eyes:

sam: Can you share the exact repro command and the perf run link?

perf-bot: Uploaded raw traces and flame graphs: https://perf.internal/runs/2115/dyn-kernel-channel-drift (profiles + nvprof + NCCL logs)

maria: Repro command we used locally (small wrapper):
```
NCCL_ALGO=RING NCCL_PROTO=LL128 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO python perf/run_inference.py \
  --model gpt-6b --tp 2 --pp 1 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --kv-cache on --dynamic-kernel on
```
Notes: single workload with mixed short and long layers due to rotated prompt lengths; we tried cold and warm KV cache.

oliver: Quick observations from the logs: when dynamic-kernel picks quantized int8 kernels for attention matmul on some layers, the all-reduce pattern flips from LL to LL128 mid-epoch (NCCL logs show channel remap and extra sync). That causes bursty NVLink traffic and a tail of stragglers.

anna: That matches the flame: lots of waiting in the compute->comm transition around layer 14 and layer 27. KV cache reuse pattern makes some GPUs finish compute earlier, then wait for allreduce. Might be an uneven seq-len packing problem.

maria: Exact numbers from the latest run (2xA100, 8 batch):
- baseline (static fp16 kernels): throughput = 12.8 tokens/s, p50 token latency = 92ms
- dynamic-kernel (auto int8 for short layers): throughput = 11.4 tokens/s, p50 = 120ms
- diff: -11% throughput, +28ms p50
We also see NCCL CYCLE stalls in the trace aligned with kernel switches.

sam: Did you try forcing NCCL_PROTO=LL (instead of LL128) to avoid channel remap? That sometimes trades off bandwidth for lower sync cost on many small collectives.

maria: Yes — quick smoke: NCCL_PROTO=LL recovered ~6% of throughput but p50 still ~110ms (so not fully mitigated). NCCL_DEBUG logs show fewer channel reassignments but more small-message overhead.

oliver: Two hypotheses: 1) dynamic kernel selection changes tensor chunking/stride which changes the size distribution of allreduces -> different NCCL decisions; 2) kernel scheduling is causing compute/comm misalignment (we're switching kernels inside the same backward/forward pass) so previously steady streams are now bursty.

anna: Actionable short experiments:
- run with batching sorted by active sequence length to reduce stragglers (pack by effective seq len)
- pin kernel choice per layer for a run (disable mid-pass switching) so all GPUs use same data shape for collectives
- try NCCL_ALGO=RING vs NCCL_ALGO=TREE and measure 95p latency

maria: I ran the pack-by-seqlen experiment: throughput improved back to 12.2 tokens/s (+7% vs dynamic default) and p50 98ms. So packing helped a lot. Patch diff incoming that adds a short-window sort in the batcher.

sam: Good. Also consider a fallback in the kernel selector that avoids switching kernel implementation if the expected all-reduce size/class would change. Like: compute expected comm-size delta and only switch if benefit > comm-cost threshold.

oliver: Agree. We can approximate comm-cost by using historical NCCL per-byte latency curve (from perf DB) and current bandwidth. Add that estimate into the kernel scoring function.

infra-bot: Alert: found 3 infra runs where NCCL channel count changes mid-run correlated with dynamic-kernel toggles (run ids: 2115021, 2115033, 2115047). Saved artifacts at https://infra.internal/nccl/2115/chan-maps.zip

anna: Another idea: break large collective into smaller pipelined allreduce windows so they align with kernel boundaries. It might add overhead but smooths traffic. Worth trying with LL128 where we get higher raw BW.

maria: I tried LL128 + per-layer kernel pinning + seqlen packing: that combination is the best so far — throughput = 12.6 tokens/s, p50 = 95ms (near baseline) but still a bit noisy at 95p. Planning a longer run to collect more samples.

sam: Can you add a microbench that reproduces just the allreduce patterns? If we script a synthetic sequence of tensor sizes that mimic kernel changes, we can test NCCL_ALGO/PROTO knobs faster than full model runs.

maria: Yep, I put a small nccl microbench script in perf/nccl_sim.py that iterates a list of sizes + interleaved compute delta to simulate kernel switching. Pushing MR now.

oliver: Let's also capture KV cache effects — when cache hits differ across ranks you get different op timings. Add a metric for per-rank kv-hit-rate and include it in traces. I suspect the earlier layers with high KV reuse are less impacted.

anna: For longer-term: consider exposing a policy in the runtime to prefer stable kernel choices in multi-GPU runs unless single-GPU latency benefit is large. We prefer predictable collectives in production.

maria: Agreed. For rollout: I'll ship the short-window seqlen packing and a flag to disable intra-pass kernel switching. We'll monitor perf dashboard and add regression alerts.

perf-bot: New perf job queued: job/2115-dyn-kernel-mitigations (will post results in ~2h).

sam: Great. If the microbench confirms, we should add an offline auto-tuner that picks kernel/collective combo per model+batch profile.

maria: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the MR link and the dashboard once the job completes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Note: when testing, try NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=COLL and NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for clearer allreduce channel logs.

oliver: Minor: add a CSV output of per-layer chosen kernel and comm-size to the perf job so we can map choices to stall points quickly.

maria: Will do. End of thread for now.
